correctness.rationale: The exact connected-subtree probability identity follows by internal-open/boundary-closed independence, and a separate exhaustive edge-configuration derivation reproduces every polynomial. Complete Prüfer census gives 1,1,2,3,6 unlabeled tree shapes for n=2,...,6. Fourteen checked polynomial factorizations prove the unique six-vertex extrema and exact critical fractions. A one-closed-edge Taylor coefficient gives the general bridge-loss identity for every n≥6, and explicit double-star and two-length-two-arm families establish both strict high-transmission failures. The fixed-order O(q²) remainder is justified by finitely many multi-edge-closure events; no infinite assertion is based on finite testing.

value.rationale: Catastrophic-outbreak tail probability is a natural ecological/epidemiological loss, not equivalent to expected outbreak size or variance. The exact first nontrivial extremal phase diagram has two distinct rational thresholds and both directions reverse. The bridge-loss expansion identifies a structural explanation for failure for every order n≥6, informing comparisons of robust network topologies. No field-data or clinical efficacy inference is drawn.
